394:                 continue
395:             string_values = line.split(",")
396:             onset_midi = (float(string_values[0]), float(string_values[1]))
397:             occurrence.append(onset_midi)
398: 
399:         # Add last occurrence and pattern to pattern_list
400:         if occurrence != []:
401:             pattern.append(occurrence)
402:         if pattern != []:
403:             pattern_list.append(pattern)
404: 
405:     return pattern_list
406: 
407: 
408: @util.deprecated(version="0.8.1", version_removed="0.9.0")
409: def load_wav(path, mono=True):
410:     """Load a .wav file as a numpy array using ``scipy.io.wavfile``.
411: 
412:     .. warning:: This function is deprecatred in mir_eval 0.8.1
413:         and will be removed in 0.9.0.
414:         We recommend using a dedicated audio IO library such as
415:         `soundfile` instead.
416: 
417:     Parameters
418:     ----------
419:     path : str or `os.Pathlike`
420:         Path to a .wav file
421:     mono : bool
422:         If the provided .wav has more than one channel, it will be
423:         converted to mono if ``mono=True``. (Default value = True)
424: 
425:     Returns
426:     -------
427:     audio_data : np.ndarray
428:         Array of audio samples, normalized to the range [-1., 1.]
429:     fs : int
430:         Sampling rate of the audio data
431:     """
432:     fs, audio_data = scipy.io.wavfile.read(path)
433:     # Make float in range [-1, 1]
434:     if audio_data.dtype == "int8":
435:         audio_data = audio_data / float(2**8)
436:     elif audio_data.dtype == "int16":
437:         audio_data = audio_data / float(2**16)
438:     elif audio_data.dtype == "int32":
439:         audio_data = audio_data / float(2**24)
440:     else:
441:         raise ValueError("Got unexpected .wav data type " "{}".format(audio_data.dtype))
442:     # Optionally convert to mono
443:     if mono and audio_data.ndim != 1:
444:         audio_data = audio_data.mean(axis=1)
445:     return audio_data, fs
446: 
447: 
448: def load_valued_intervals(filename, delimiter=r"\s+", comment="#"):
449:     r"""Import valued intervals from an annotation file. The file should
450:     consist of three columns: Two consisting of numeric values corresponding to
451:     start and end time of each interval and a third, also of numeric values,
452:     corresponding to the value of each interval. This is primarily useful for
453:     processing events which span a duration and have a numeric value, such as
454:     piano-roll notes which have an onset, offset, and a pitch value.
455: 
456:     Parameters
457:     ----------
458:     filename : str or `os.Pathlike`
459:         Path to the annotation file
460: 
461:     delimiter : str
462:         Separator regular expression.
463:         By default, lines will be split by any amount of whitespace.
464: 
465:     comment : str or None
466:         Comment regular expression.
467:         Any lines beginning with this string or pattern will be ignored.
468: 
469:         Setting to `None` disables comments.
470: 
471:     Returns
472:     -------
473:     intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n_events, 2)
474:         Array of event start and end times
475:     values : np.ndarray, shape=(n_events,)
476:         Array of values
477: 
478:     """
479:     # Use our universal function to load in the events
480:     starts, ends, values = load_delimited(
481:         filename, [float, float, float], delimiter=delimiter, comment=comment
482:     )
483:     # Stack into an interval matrix
484:     intervals = np.array([starts, ends]).T
485:     # Validate them, but throw a warning in place of an error
486:     try:
487:         util.validate_intervals(intervals)
488:     except ValueError as error:
489:         warnings.warn(error.args[0])
490: 
491:     # return values as np.ndarray
492:     values = np.array(values)
493: 
494:     return intervals, values
495: 
496: 
497: def load_key(filename, delimiter=r"\s+", comment="#"):
498:     r"""Load key labels from an annotation file. The file should
499:     consist of two string columns: One denoting the key scale degree
500:     (semitone), and the other denoting the mode (major or minor).  The file
501:     should contain only one row.
502: 
503:     Parameters
504:     ----------
505:     filename : str or `os.Pathlike`
506:         Path to the annotation file
507: 
508:     delimiter : str
509:         Separator regular expression.
510:         By default, lines will be split by any amount of whitespace.
511: 
512:     comment : str or None
513:         Comment regular expression.
514:         Any lines beginning with this string or pattern will be ignored.
515: 
516:         Setting to `None` disables comments.
517: 
518:     Returns
519:     -------
520:     key : str
521:         Key label, in the form ``'(key) (mode)'``
522: 
523:     """
524:     # Use our universal function to load the key and mode strings
525:     scale, mode = load_delimited(
526:         filename, [str, str], delimiter=delimiter, comment=comment
527:     )
528:     if len(scale) != 1:
529:         raise ValueError("Key file should contain only one line.")
530:     scale, mode = scale[0], mode[0]
531:     # Join with a space
532:     key_string = f"{scale} {mode}"
533:     # Validate them, but throw a warning in place of an error
534:     try:
535:         key.validate_key(key_string)
536:     except ValueError as error:
537:         warnings.warn(error.args[0])
538: 
539:     return key_string
540:

542: def load_tempo(filename, delimiter=r"\s+", comment="#"):
543:     r"""Load tempo estimates from an annotation file in MIREX format.
544:     The file should consist of three numeric columns: the first two
545:     correspond to tempo estimates (in beats-per-minute), and the third
546:     denotes the relative confidence of the first value compared to the
547:     second (in the range [0, 1]). The file should contain only one row.
548: 
549:     Parameters
